provenance_key.S: search-sourced: the link came from a search result and is confirmed by the weekly link check
provenance_key.K: background knowledge: a lead, confirmed only by the weekly link check

sources.name: UK Youth Parliament
sources.what: The elected voice of 11 to 18 year olds across the UK, run by the National Youth Agency.
sources.use: Find your MYP, the manifesto and the annual Make Your Mark ballot.

sources.name: Scottish Youth Parliament
sources.what: The democratically elected voice of Scotland's young people, with a 2026 to 2031 manifesto.
sources.use: Check elections and the Scottish manifesto before campaigning in Scotland.

sources.name: Welsh Youth Parliament
sources.what: Sixty members aged 11 to 17, elected by constituency and partner organisations, meeting at the Senedd.
sources.use: See priorities the Welsh Government has agreed to consider routinely.

sources.name: Northern Ireland Youth Assembly
sources.what: Ninety members selected at random so every constituency and community is represented, chaired by the Assembly Speaker.
sources.use: Search the Assembly site for the Youth Assembly and its committees.

sources.name: Youth Select Committee
sources.what: Twelve MYPs who run a televised inquiry each year; the 2025 to 2026 inquiry reported on PSHE in March 2026.
sources.use: Read the PSHE report and the Government's response before lobbying on curriculum.

sources.name: UK Parliament petitions
sources.what: Petitions to the UK Government and Parliament: 10,000 signatures for a response, 100,000 to be considered for debate.
sources.use: Check thresholds and the status of any petition you are backing.

sources.name: Register to vote
sources.what: The official route to register: from 14 in Scotland and Wales, and from 16 in England and Northern Ireland.
sources.use: Register before an election deadline; it takes about five minutes online.
sources.note: Age rules differ by nation and are changing with the Representation of the People Bill.

sources.name: Representation of the People Bill
sources.what: The Bill that would extend the vote to 16 and 17 year olds in all UK elections.
sources.use: Track each stage of the Bill on Parliament's own record.

sources.name: Votes at 16 policy summary
sources.what: The Government's explanation of extending the vote to 16 and 17 year olds, updated May 2026.
sources.use: Quote what the Government itself says the Bill does.

sources.name: Electoral Commission: young people's views on politics and voting
sources.what: 2026 research on how young people see politics and voting.
sources.use: Ground arguments about youth turnout in the regulator's evidence.

sources.name: Children's Commissioner for England
sources.what: Promotes and protects children's rights in England; publishes the School and College Census and mental health reports.
sources.use: Cite her reports when making the case to ministers in England.

sources.name: Children and Young People's Commissioner Scotland
sources.what: Protects children's rights in Scotland, where the UNCRC is incorporated into law.
sources.use: Check what is legally enforceable in Scotland before you campaign there.

sources.name: Children's Commissioner for Wales
sources.what: Promotes and protects children's rights in Wales; three-year strategy for 2026 to 2029.
sources.use: Use the strategy and election resources for Welsh campaigns.

sources.name: NI Commissioner for Children and Young People
sources.what: Safeguards and promotes children's rights in Northern Ireland, including mental health service reviews.
sources.use: Cite NICCY's reviews when campaigning in Northern Ireland.

sources.name: UNICEF UK: the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
sources.what: The full UNCRC, article by article, in plain language.
sources.use: Name the article your campaign rests on.

sources.name: Childline
sources.what: Free, confidential support for anyone under 19, by phone, 1-2-1 chat and email, run by the NSPCC. British Sign Language users can reach a counsellor through SignVideo.
sources.use: Call, chat or email about anything, at any time.

sources.name: Report Remove
sources.what: Childline and the Internet Watch Foundation's tool for under 18s to get a nude image or video of themselves removed.
sources.use: Use it if an image of you has been shared, or you are worried it will be.

sources.name: CEOP Safety Centre
sources.what: The National Crime Agency's route for children and parents to report online sexual abuse or grooming.
sources.use: Report an adult behaving inappropriately towards a child online. Not for bullying.

sources.name: NSPCC Helpline
sources.what: Advice for adults worried about a child.
sources.use: For the adult ally who is worried about a young person.

sources.name: Samaritans
sources.what: Any age, any problem, free from any phone, open 24 hours. Welsh Language Line 0808 164 0123, every day 7pm to 11pm.
sources.use: Call any time, day or night.

sources.name: Shout
sources.what: Free 24/7 text support for anyone in the UK.
sources.use: Text if you would rather not speak to anyone.

sources.name: The Mix
sources.what: Support for under 25s on mental health, money, work and relationships, with 24/7 crisis text support.
sources.use: Text for urgent support; its old phone helpline has closed.

sources.name: YoungMinds
sources.what: Youth mental health information, plus a helpline for the adult supporting you. Not a crisis service.
sources.use: Point a parent or carer to the Parents Helpline; hours vary week to week.

sources.name: Youth Access
sources.what: A network of free local youth advice and counselling services, with a find-help directory.
sources.use: Find free advice or counselling near you.

sources.name: NHS 111
sources.what: Urgent help when it is not an emergency, including urgent mental health support. In an emergency call 999.
sources.use: Use it for urgent mental health support when you cannot wait.

sources.name: Minimum wage rates
sources.what: Rates in force from 1 April 2026: £12.71 (21 and over), £10.85 (18 to 20), £8 (under 18 and apprentices).
sources.use: Check you are paid at least the legal minimum for your age.

sources.name: Minimum wage rates for April 2027
sources.what: Announced 28 October 2026: £13.21 (21 and over) and £11.27 (18 to 20) from 1 April 2027.
sources.use: Plan for the next rise; it is not in force until April 2027.

sources.name: Youth Futures Foundation
sources.what: The What Works centre for youth employment; publishes quarterly NEET analysis and a data dashboard.
sources.use: Use its NEET trends when arguing about jobs and training.

sources.name: ONS: young people not in education, employment or training
sources.what: The official quarterly NEET estimate for 16 to 24 year olds.
sources.use: Quote the latest official figure, with its quarter.
sources.note: Link built from the bulletin's known address; the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Youth Matters: Your National Youth Strategy
sources.what: England's first national youth strategy in over two decades, published 10 December 2025 and shaped by over 14,000 young people.
sources.use: Hold the Government to its own commitments, chapter by chapter.

sources.name: NYA: National Youth Strategy hub
sources.what: The youth work sector's guide to what the strategy commits and what is next.
sources.use: See how the strategy reaches youth services in your area.

sources.name: CMS Committee: National Youth Strategy one year on
sources.what: A Commons inquiry into progress on the strategy: services, workforce, funding and accountability.
sources.use: Submit evidence while the inquiry is open.

sources.name: Work and Pensions Committee: youth employment, education and training
sources.what: A Commons inquiry opened 8 January 2026 into young people not earning or learning.
sources.use: Read the evidence sessions before campaigning on jobs.

sources.name: ICO Children's code (Age appropriate design)
sources.what: The statutory code of 15 standards for online services likely to be used by under 18s.
sources.use: Check any app or site a campaign asks young people to use.

sources.name: Ofcom: protecting children online
sources.what: The Online Safety Act regulator; its Protection of Children Codes have applied since 25 July 2025.
sources.use: Understand what platforms must now do to protect under 18s.

sources.name: Become
sources.what: The national charity for children in care and young care leavers.
sources.use: Make sure care-experienced young people's views reach a campaign.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Carers Trust: young carers
sources.what: Support and services for young carers and young adult carers.
sources.use: Plan campaign activity young carers can actually fit around caring.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Refugee Council
sources.what: Support for refugees and people seeking asylum, including children and young people.
sources.use: Hear from young refugees, safely and without exposing their status.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Friends, Families and Travellers
sources.what: A national charity working with Gypsy, Roma and Traveller communities.
sources.use: Reach Gypsy, Roma and Traveller young people on their own terms.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Council for Disabled Children
sources.what: The umbrella body for the disabled children's sector in England, with a young people's participation network.
sources.use: Involve disabled young people and those with SEND from the start.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Just Like Us
sources.what: A charity for LGBT+ young people in schools.
sources.use: Make campaign spaces safe for LGBT+ young people.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: National Careers Service
sources.what: Free careers information, advice and guidance in England.
sources.use: Explore jobs, courses and apprenticeships, and talk to an adviser.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: My World of Work
sources.what: Skills Development Scotland's careers service for young people in Scotland.
sources.use: Plan your next step after school in Scotland.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Young Scot
sources.what: Scotland's national youth information and citizenship charity.
sources.use: Find opportunities, rewards and ways to have your say in Scotland.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Careers Wales
sources.what: The all-age careers service for Wales, in Welsh and English.
sources.use: Get careers guidance in Welsh or English.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Meic
sources.what: The information, advice and advocacy helpline for children and young people in Wales, in Welsh and English.
sources.use: Talk to someone in Welsh or English about anything.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: nidirect Careers
sources.what: The Department for the Economy's careers service for Northern Ireland.
sources.use: Get careers advice in Northern Ireland.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Education Authority Youth Service
sources.what: Northern Ireland's statutory youth service, including youth participation programmes.
sources.use: Find youth services and participation routes in Northern Ireland.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: RNID
sources.what: The national charity for deaf people and people with hearing loss; campaigned for the BSL Act 2022 and the Northern Ireland Sign Language Act.
sources.use: Check accessibility advice for deaf participants.

sources.name: National Deaf Children's Society
sources.what: The national charity for deaf children and young people and their families, with youth participation opportunities.
sources.use: Find deaf-led youth voices and support for families.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: UK Youth
sources.what: A national charity supporting a network of youth organisations and clubs across the UK.
sources.use: Find youth clubs and organisations in your area.

sources.name: YouthLink Scotland
sources.what: The national agency for youth work in Scotland.
sources.use: Connect with youth work in Scotland.

sources.name: Scouts
sources.what: Uniformed youth groups for 4 to 25 year olds across the UK, including democracy and citizenship badges.
sources.use: Find a local group and its democracy activities.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Girlguiding
sources.what: Uniformed groups for girls and young women across the UK.
sources.use: Find a local unit and its youth voice work.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: #iwill movement
sources.what: A movement for youth social action; the National Youth Strategy funds #iwill ambassadors.
sources.use: Find social action opportunities and ambassadors.
sources.note: A lead from background knowledge until the weekly link check confirms it.

sources.name: Code Club
sources.what: Free coding clubs for school-aged young people, run by the Raspberry Pi Foundation, with hundreds of free step-by-step projects.
sources.use: Join a club near you, start one at school or a library, or volunteer: you do not need coding experience to run one.

sources.name: CoderDojo
sources.what: Free, volunteer-led community coding clubs for young people, part of the Raspberry Pi Foundation alongside Code Club.
sources.use: Find a Dojo, including library clubs such as CoderDojo Scotland in Glasgow, or mentor at one.

sources.name: Stemettes
sources.what: Award-winning social enterprise inspiring girls, young women and non-binary young people aged 5 to 25 into STEAM, with events, clubs, mentoring and a youth advisory network.
sources.use: Free events, the Student to Stemette mentoring programme for 15 to 25 year olds, and volunteer roles for young people.

sources.name: TechFirst (DSIT)
sources.what: The government's flagship tech skills programme. Its youth strand, TechYouth, aims to reach one million 11 to 18 year olds; it took over CyberFirst from 1 September 2026, and DSIT now runs the girls' competition.
sources.use: Look for TechYouth activities through your school or college, the TechFirst Girls Competition, and TechGrad scholarships for later study.

sources.name: NCSC cyber skills
sources.what: The National Cyber Security Centre still leads the cyber pathway inside TechFirst, after CyberFirst moved across on 1 September 2026.
sources.use: Cyber security courses, bursary information and the history of the CyberFirst Girls Competition.

sources.name: Technovation Girls
sources.what: A free global programme where teams of girls aged 8 to 18 build an app or other digital solution to a problem in their community, with a mentor.
sources.use: Register a team for the 2026-27 season, or volunteer as a mentor, judge or local ambassador.

sources.name: The Big Bang Competition
sources.what: EngineeringUK's free competition for 11 to 19 year olds in state-funded education, home education or community groups, with UK Young Engineer, Technologist and Scientist awards.
sources.use: Enter a STEM project; finalists show their work at The Big Bang Fair in Birmingham.

sources.name: Apps for Good
sources.what: An education charity whose free courses help young people use tech, including AI, to solve problems they care about, with an annual showcase.
sources.use: Ask a teacher to run a course or computing club; enter the Showcase.

sources.name: Open City Accelerate
sources.what: A free programme for 16 to 18 year olds from under-represented backgrounds exploring careers in architecture, landscape, planning and engineering, with workshops and professional mentoring.
sources.use: Apply when the next round opens (the 2026-27 round has closed); architects can volunteer as DBS-checked mentors.

sources.name: STEM Ambassadors
sources.what: A UK-wide network of volunteers from STEM jobs who visit schools, colleges, clubs and youth groups, run by STEM Learning and supported by UKRI.
sources.use: Invite a STEM Ambassador into a club or youth group, or become one (with a background check, such as PVG in Scotland).

sources.name: WISE (part of the IET)
sources.what: The campaign for women in science, technology and engineering, part of the IET since 2025, which publishes workforce data for women in core STEM roles.
sources.use: Workforce statistics, role models and resources for schools and employers.

sources.name: EngineeringUK
sources.what: A not-for-profit working to bring more young people from every background into engineering and technology. It publishes workforce data and runs The Big Bang.
sources.use: Gender and diversity data for engineering and tech, and the Tomorrow's Engineers Code.

sources.name: Government Digital and Data Profession Capability Framework
sources.what: The government's description of every digital and data role and the skills for each level, including seven architecture roles: business, data, enterprise, network, security, solution and technical architect.
sources.use: See what each role does, from trainee level up, and the skills to build for it.

sources.name: TechTrack apprenticeship (GDS)
sources.what: A Level 4 digital apprenticeship led by the Government Digital Service, for business analysts, software developers, DevOps engineers and cyber security technologists, open to people outside the Civil Service too.
sources.use: Register interest to hear when the next cohort opens.

sources.name: Civil Service apprenticeships
sources.what: Apprenticeships across government departments, from digital support to IT service management, advertised on Find an apprenticeship and Civil Service Jobs.
sources.use: Search Find an apprenticeship for 'Civil Service' roles near you.

sources.name: Civil Service Fast Stream
sources.what: The government's graduate development programme, with schemes including Digital, Cyber Security and Science and Engineering; applications open each autumn.
sources.use: Check the schemes and the next application window; serving civil servants may apply without a degree.

sources.name: Fast Stream Summer Internship Programme
sources.what: A paid two-month summer internship in a government department for people from lower socio-economic backgrounds, with a Fast Pass into the Fast Stream after a positive appraisal.
sources.use: Apply in the autumn for the following summer; you can take part once.

sources.name: Impact: The Local Government Graduate Programme
sources.what: The Local Government Association's two-year graduate programme in councils (formerly the NGDP), with placements across council services.
sources.use: Applications reopen each October; there is also a planning pathway.

sources.name: NHS apprenticeships
sources.what: Apprenticeships into many of the NHS's more than 350 careers, including digital and data roles such as data technician.
sources.use: Explore roles on Step into the NHS and Health Careers.

sources.name: Northern Ireland Civil Service apprenticeships
sources.what: NICS trainee and apprenticeship schemes, including ICT apprenticeships in networking or software development and an Operational Delivery Apprenticeship.
sources.use: Watch NICS recruitment for the next schemes.

sources.name: Apprenticeships in Scotland
sources.what: Foundation Apprenticeships alongside school, Modern Apprenticeships at work, and Graduate Apprenticeships to degree level, including digital frameworks.
sources.use: Search apprenticeships.scot and My World of Work.

sources.name: Jobs Growth Wales+
sources.what: A Welsh Government programme, part of the Young Person's Guarantee, giving 16 to 19 year olds not in education, employment or training training, work placements and an allowance.
sources.use: Contact Working Wales to be referred.

sources.name: GCHQ early careers
sources.what: Early-career routes at the UK's intelligence, cyber and security agency, including a paid Cyber Insights Summer School and software engineering degree apprenticeships.
sources.use: Look for the summer school and apprenticeship windows; security vetting and nationality rules apply.

sources.name: Government Security Profession careers
sources.what: Careers and learning in government security, including cyber, with routes such as the Cyber Security Fast Stream.
sources.use: See the roles and the early-career routes into them.

sources.name: Innovate UK Young Innovators
sources.what: Innovate UK's award for 18 to 30 year olds with a business idea: a grant, a living allowance for two days a week and a year of mentoring.
sources.use: Watch for the next round; follow-on Next Steps awards support the most successful.

sources.name: CREST Awards (British Science Association)
sources.what: The British Science Association's hands-on STEM project awards for ages 3 to 19, at levels from Discovery to Gold; free for all young people in Scotland.
sources.use: Turn a science or engineering project into a recognised award, alongside a Big Bang entry if you like.

sources.name: Experience AI
sources.what: Free AI literacy lessons for 11 to 14 year olds from the Raspberry Pi Foundation and Google DeepMind, covering how AI works, bias, privacy and using AI responsibly; usable in coding clubs too.
sources.use: Ask a teacher or club leader to run the lessons.

sources.name: British Science Week
sources.what: A ten-day celebration of science, technology, engineering and maths run by the British Science Association; 5 to 14 March 2027, themed Creativity.
sources.use: Free resource packs, a poster competition and grants for schools and community groups.
